item.title: No. 6 Texas women pull away from No. 19 Ohio State
item.description: Breya Cunningham put up a season-high 24 points and 13 rebounds to help No. 6 Texas defeat No. 19 Ohio State 75-61 on Nov. 22 in Fort Worth, Texas. Jayda Clark tallied 15 points, seven rebounds and five assists for the Longhorns (6-0), while Texas star Madison Booker scored all 12 of her points in the second half after shooting 0 for 5 and committing five turnovers before halftime. Texas shot 35.8% overall and 2 for 11 from 3-point range but hit 25 of 26 free throws (96.2%). Cunningham and Booker each went 6 for 6 from the line, as Texas won every quarter and scored the first 16 points of the fourth quarter to blow open a reasonably close game. Jaloni Cambridge scored 27 points for Ohio State (5-2), and Ava Watson and Sydney Mobley added 8 each. The Buckeyes scored 29 points off 20 Texas turnovers to stay in striking distance until the fourth quarter. They fell behind 75-48 before scoring the final 13 points of the game. Texas won the battle on the boards 49-33 and scored 21 second-chance points off 20 offensive rebounds. item.title: Victor Wembanyama's latest 50-point game came with an ethical dilemma
item.description: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) takes a 3-point shot during the second quarter of an NBA game against the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. The Spurs won 114-91. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) With 6:27 remaining Saturday and the Spurs ahead by 23 points, Victor Wembanyama rose for a step-back 3-pointer from the right arc. From his post on the sidelines, Spurs coach Mitch Johnson looked on with pit in his stomach, as if his job depended on the shot going in. Which, perhaps, it did. "I was just hoping he got to 50 when he did," Johnson said. With one final swish, Wembanyama gave Johnson his wish. The shot pushed Wembanyama to an even 50 points, putting the finishing touch on another game for the ages by the All-Star center in a 114-91 blowout victory over the Pelicans. It also allowed Johnson to get his franchise player off the floor and to the safety of the Spurs' bench without an argument. "It would have been hard to take him out that close to 50," Johnson said. Not for the first time this season, Wembanyama's final stat line Saturday looked like something that fell out of Wilt Chamberlain's Basketball Reference page: 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals. Wembanyama didn't arrive at the Frost Bank Center with any grand designs on producing a box score never before recorded in NBA history. It just sort of happened that way. "They just come when we play the right way as a team," the 7-foot-4 Frenchman said. "I just want to stack them up. Hopefully there is many more coming." Before Saturday, no player in the NBA this season had put up a game of at least 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals. Wembanyama had that by halftime. His night began with a 17-point first quarter, a career high. He ended it with the third 50-point game of his career. Perhaps the most eye-popping part of Wembanyama's latest eruption was that it wasn't even his best performance of the season. That distinction belongs to his 52-point, 24-rebound, eight-block opus in a Nov. 4 victory over Dallas. "Sometimes you can feel a special game brewing," Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox said. "That first quarter you could definitely feel it coming. We try to make some of his baskets easier, and when he does those special things you feel those special things." Thanks to his most recent outburst, Wembanyama will head into Monday's game at Sacramento averaging 29.9 points per game, third-most in the league behind the Los Angeles Lakers' Luka Doncic and Oklahoma City's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. Propelled by Wembanyama, the Spurs won for the 14 th time in 15 games, improving their season record to 14-3 to equal the Lakers and Philadelphia 76ers for the best in the league. item.title: Well, That’s Better: Marquette 106, Chicago State 62
item.description: Michael Phillips had himself a nice outing against the Cougars. | Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images When Colin Porter missed a three-pointer with 14:10 left to go in the first half, that went into the scorebooks as Marquette’s first missed field goal of the game. Yes, nearly six straight minutes without missing a shot. Your score at the time: Marquette 22, Chicago State 10. The Golden Eagles had just answered a 5-0 CSU burst with nine straight before the Cougars cashed in a three-pointer to break up that run. For the next few minutes, it was actually a back and forth basketball game. From the 12 minute mark of the first half until there was under eight minutes left, neither team scored two buckets in a row. That left Marquette up just 12 points even though they had led by as many as 17 at one point. And then Marquette discovered the EVAPORATE button. 10 straight for the Golden Eagles, with Royce Parham hitting two three-pointers along the way. Then a free throw from CSU’s Mike Price, then a three from Michael Phillips, then a layup from CSU’s Foday Sheriff, then another 10 straight points from Marquette to end the half. 10-0 run to end the half, or 13-2 if you prefer, or 23-3 if you prefer. Marquette by 32, 57-25, at intermission. The lead hit 40 for the first time on a triple from Phillips as part of a 9-0 run in the second half as MU blew the margin out to 75-31 with 15:03 to play. That 44 point gap would be the largest lead of the game for Marquette as Chicago State did managed to shave some space off of that, first with an immediate 8-0 run, and back-to-back three-pointers from Davius Loury got the Cougars as close as 34. That’s the most that Marquette allowed, and then they closed the game on an 18-8 run. Never more than five at a time, but that’s how they ended up back at 44 to end it. For historic purposes: Ian Miletic got Marquette over the century mark with a three-pointer with 1:38 to go, and that shot tied the program record for threes by a team in a game. Miletic then broke that record with Marquette’s 19th three-pointer of the game with 54 seconds left. That's a NEW SCHOOL RECORD for three pointers made with 19!!🔥🔥 @Ian7Miletic with his third triple in the second half. #MUBB | #WeAreMarquette pic.twitter.com/evo166QA4i — Marquette Men’s Basketball (@MarquetteMBB) November 22, 2026 Your leading scorer here was Adrien Stevens, who put up 18 points on 6-for-11 shooting, with four of his five misses coming as part of his 5-for-9 three-point shooting on the day. Royce Parham had 16, Sananda Fru and Michael Phillips both had 13, and Nigel James added 11. Nolan Minessale’s five rebounds led the Golden Eagles in that column, and James had seven assists in 20 foul-and-margin shortened minutes. In case you were wondering: Marquette shot 75% on two-pointers here, which is a marked improvement on what they’ve looked like in general this season. They also grabbed 67% of their rare misses and limited Chicago State to just 39% of their misses

item.title: ‘The sweetest interaction’: Taylor Swift celebrates Travis Kelce touchdown with niece in adorable video
item.description: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports Taylor Swift was back at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday to watch her husband, Travis Kelce, and the Kansas City Chiefs take on the Arizona Cardinals. And this time, she had plenty of family with her in the suite, including one of Kelce’s nieces. When Kelce caught his second touchdown of the day, cameras captured Swift hugging and celebrating with Wyatt Kelce, the oldest daughter of Jason and Kylie Kelce. Needless to say, the sweet moment quickly made the rounds on social media, and Swift’s fans couldn’t get enough of it. Kelce gave them plenty to cheer about early on. He caught an 8-yard touchdown pass from Patrick Mahomes in the first quarter, then hauled in a 22-yard score late in the second quarter as the Chiefs built a 27-7 halftime lead. It was after that second touchdown that Swift was shown celebrating with Wyatt, who was all smiles as her aunt wrapped her up in a hug. item.title: ‘Massive loser’: DK Metcalf’s nightmare season continues with ejection
item.description: Oct 12, 2025; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf (4) makes a catch for a touchdown during the fourth quarter at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images DK Metcalf was already having a disastrous 2026 season coming into Sunday, and the Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver didn’t do anything this afternoon to help his cause. Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter of today’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles after earning his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. The two-time Pro Bowler got into it with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean and a few of his teammates during his final confrontation, finishing the day with one reception for two yards, two personal fouls and one ejecction. Acquired before the 2025 season in a trade with the Seattle Seahawks, Metcalf has not lived up to the lucrative contract extension Pittsburgh gave him. In 10 games this fall, he’s recorded only 35 receptions for 432 yards and two touchdowns. ‘ Hard to find someone having a worse season’ Metcalf’s ejection elicited plenty of online reaction, including from some fed-up Steelers fans. “ There has never been a bigger loser to play for the Steelers than DK Metcalf . Just a gigantic, massive loser,” said Pittsburgh-based sportswriter Adam Gretz . “ Hard to find someone having a worse season than DK Metcalf . Guy is absolutely sabotaging his own offense. Steelers just got better by him getting ejected,” added NFL writer Sam Monson . “ Trading DK Metcalf when he did was one of John Schneider’s greatest moves as #Seahawks GM,” said BBC Sheffield’s Rob Staton . “ DK Metcalf and Aaron Rodgers are the worst QB-WR marriage in the league,” chimed in Yahoo Sports’ Josh Norris. “ The Steelers traded away a “problem” WR to go out and trade for DK Metcalf, w ho costed them a 2nd, $132M extension, is much worse than George Pickens + is even more of a problem WR. Hilarious franchise decision making,” said Matt of Six Rings of Steel . More punishment incoming? Today was the third ejection of Metcalf’s career, and KOA Colorado’s Benjamin Allbright tweeted moments ago that it could cost him his next game as well. “ League source suggests that DK Metcalf could be seeing an additional suspension and miss the Broncos game on Friday,” Allbright said . “ Metcalf has been ejected in two previous games and is considered a repeat offender.” The Steelers are scheduled to take on the Broncos at 3 p.m. ET on Black Friday. item.title: Liverpool vs Man United player ratings: Two 9/10s inspire as Mauricio Pochettino endures nightmare bow
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino endured a dismal start to his tenure at Manchester United as Liverpool ran riot in a 4-0 victory against their relegation-threatened rivals. A whirlwind week for the former Argentina international ended in familiar disappointment for the struggling visitors, whose hopes of a new manager bounce were decisively crushed during a nightmare opening 13 minutes at Anfield. Dominik Szoboszlai put the hosts ahead with a fierce free-kick after defender Leny Yoro was sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity inside just eight minutes, before Florian Wirtz ’s smart finish quickly put Pochettino’s side further behind. United managed to temporarily stem the tide courtesy of crucial Senne Lammens saves, last-ditch defending, and wayward finishing, but Andoni Iraola’s side redoubled their efforts after the interval. Pochettino’s 10 men were frankly fortunate that Liverpool only added two more goals through Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz, such was the overwhelming nature of their dominance. Here are how the players rated at Anfield: Liverpool Alisson - 7 Smart stop to deny Fernandes when Man United started knocking at the door in the first half, alive to the situation after not being required in the early stages. Barely got a touch after the break, until being called until action in stoppage time to deny Fernandes consolation. Ronald Araujo - 8 His through ball for Isak was more of a hooked clearance than a calculated lofted pass, but it still caused the chaos required to get Yoro sent off. Always willing to get in the challenge. Subbed. item.description: Oct 7, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago White Sox pitcher Davis Martin (65) throws a pitch during the ninth inning against the Cleveland Guardians in game three of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Rate Field. Mandatory Credit: Ma… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Lewis Masella, Site Editor The Chicago White Sox shipped veteran right-handers Luis Castillo and Davis Martin to the Colorado Rockies in a four-player swap on Thursday. The trade means the entirety of Castillo’s remaining $22.75 million guarantee for 2027, after posting an 8.42 ERA down the stretch for Chicago, will now be paid by the Rockies. GM Chris Getz parting with Martin, the longest-tenured player who posted a 3.95 ERA over 146 innings, was seen as a ruthless move, but the Rockies weren’t willing to take Castillo without Martin. That is the price of doing business in the modern baseball market. ‎However, Martin’s lingering right calf issue may be one reason Getz agreed to trade him. It is hard to predict whether the 29-year-old will deliver 2026-level production next year, given that injuries have been his biggest letdown over the past three years. Now, with roughly $25 million off the White Sox payroll, two sudden openings in Will Venable’s starting rotation need to be filled. This is when the real work begins because replacing Castillo and Martin isn’t a simple one-for-one swap. It requires balancing immediate playoff-caliber innings with extensive experience in commanding the zone, and already-made pitchers with an illustrious career record. item.description: In past regular seasons, the Boston Celtics have generally churned out win after win, especially under head coach Joe Mazzulla. However, after resting multiple key players against the struggling Sacramento Kings on Saturday night and falling to them, 97-96, the C's are at risk of losing four games in a row. That'd be enough for Boston's longest losing streak since the 2020-21 season, which was back when de facto Celtics general manager Brad Stevens was still the head coach of the Green Team. Such a skid can be avoided if the 11-5 Celtics are able to topple the 8-8 Golden State Warriors on Sunday evening in San Francisco. The C's may be tired because they're playing on the second night of a back-to-back — their fourth time doing so this November — but attempting to bounce back from arguably their worst defeat of the season could serve as motivation. Although, one could say the same about the Warriors, who are currently on a five-game losing streak (the longest active slide in the Western Conference) that's coincided with the injury absence of star point guard Stephen Curry. The future Hall of Famer won't return versus the Celtics, but star forward Jayson Tatum could take the floor again for Boston after resting on Saturday. item.title: Carlos Alcaraz adds ATP Finals title to glittering trophy cabinet
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Spanish tennis player Carlos Alcaraz celebrates defeating US' Ben Shelton during their men's singles semifinal match of the 2026 Nitto ATP Finals, an international tennis match in Turin. (is associated with: «Carlos Alcaraz adds ATP Finals title to glittering trophy cabinet») Mickael Chavet/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa Carlos Alcaraz made more history with a maiden ATP Finals title after a straight-sets win over Alexander Zverev. A 6-2 7-6 (7) triumph in Turin enabled seven-time major champion Alcaraz to follow in the footsteps of Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic by becoming the fourth male player to win the end-of-season tournament along with each four grand slams in their career. Alcaraz had finished runner-up to Jannik Sinner in 2025 and lost twice to current world number one Zverev previously in the competition, but showed why many still proclaim the Spaniard to be the best player in the world after an impressive two-hour-and-two-minutes victory. With strapping on his left leg and after a gruelling three-set battle with Ben Shelton on Saturday, Alcaraz set about becoming the first player of the week to take a set off French Open and US Open champion Zverev. Top seed Zverev was forced to dig deep to hold on his first service game, but was broken three times during a one-sided opening set. Alcaraz broke again to move 2-1 up in the second before a 4-2 lead was established. However, Alcaraz let slip his advantage and a topsy-turvy tie-break followed between the first and second seed. After Alcaraz claimed an early break, Zverev reeled off six points in a row, but failed to take three set points. Then at the second time of asking, after one match point was saved, Alcaraz produced a bullet backhand to defeat Zverev and he duly collapsed to the ground after winning the 30th title of his extraordinary career and sixth of an injury-hit 2026. "This trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me," Alcaraz said on-court. "Today's final, I needed to put the three c's that my grandpa always tells me that I have to give every time that I step on the court for every match and every practice. "He's watching at home, so I just want to say I love you to my grandparents. In Spanish it's 'Cabeza, corazon, cajones', in English it is 'head, heart, balls', so I think today that was about it."

item.title: I feel the pain: Pochettino takes responsibility for Man Utd hammering
item.description: Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Liverpool and Manchester United at the Anfield. (is associated with: «I feel the pain: Pochettino takes responsibility for Man Utd hammering») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Mauricio Pochettino accepted full responsibility for the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool as he endured the worst debut by a Manchester United manager in 100 years. Not since player-manager Lal Hilditch lost 4-0 to Bolton in October 1926 had a new boss endured such a chastening start, which left the club 19th in the Premier League, two points away from climbing out of the bottom three. But while the head coach said he took full ownership of the result, he felt the eighth-minute red card shown to Leny Yoro changed the course of the game. The defender's dismissal for denying Alexander Isak a goalscoring opportunity following Matthijs de Ligt's mistake allowed Dominik Szoboszlai to score from the resulting free-kick. A brilliant twisting volley from Florian Wirtz, his fifth goal in four games for club and country, doubled the lead and while Liverpool should have added plenty more, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz compounded a chastening evening for Pochettino in the second half. It proved too much for some fans in the visiting section with police called to deal with a disturbance with one man being led away in handcuffs. "It is painful because it is 4-0 but we play more than 80 minutes with 10 men. I take responsibility for that, no worries," said Pochettino, who argued a challenge by Jeremy Jacquet on Bryan Mbeumo before the red card should have resulted in a penalty. "We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is true. "You need to look at the circumstance because it is so easy to talk so cheap. We lose one game; we are not going to lose more than one game how we lose today. "We have a lot of work to do and we take responsibility. We feel the pain but the thing is to keep working." United have conceded 23 goals in 11 league matches and Pochettino's decision to hand De Ligt his first Premier League start in a year drew scrutiny, which only increased with the defender's performance. "The team concede because the balance is not so good and I take responsibility for that," said the Argentinian. "He (De Ligt) was training, he played in the Champions League before the international duty and when we arrived we saw the combinations." Asked whether he had inherited a relegation battle, Pochettino added: "Still a lot of games to play. We need to accept the reality and we need to be united and all together. "We feel disappointed because it is clear after what happened (Yoro's red card) happened the plan was in the bin. item.title: Leeds United Have Strong Chance Of Striking This Striker Bargain: Should Farke Push For Him?
item.description: Leeds United Have Strong Chance Of Striking This Striker Bargain: Should Farke Push For Him? Leeds United have a strong chance of signing Stuttgart striker Ermedin Demirović, according to Sport Witness , which cites Tuttosport. Leeds pursued the 28-year-old over the summer, and the report says his own eagerness to leave now gives them an edge. Demirović has agreed to no new contract and his current deal expires in 2028, so Tuttosport expect his summer valuation of €30m (roughly £26m) to fall sharply. Milan are the main obstacle. The report says their incoming sporting director, Markus Krösche, knows the Bosnian forward well, and other Premier League clubs are interested. He arrives in good form. Tuttosport credits him with nine goals in 15 appearances in the Bundesliga and Champions League this season, and FotMob ‘s data supports the finishing, with 4.76 expected goals from nine league games. His limits are clear. He wins only 25.6% of his aerial duels and ranks low for touches and chances created, so he finishes moves rather than starting them. That profile matters because of how Daniel Farke sets Leeds up. His 3-5-2 needs two forwards, yet Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who scored 14 Premier League goals last season, has battled foot trouble since the 1-1 draw with Manchester United in October. Leeds now sit sixth after the demolition of Chelsea, but they scored once or not at all in each of their last six league games leading up to this. Should Leeds United push for Demirović in January? STUTTGART, GERMANY – OCTOBER 23: Ermedin Demirovic of VfB Stuttgart celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Bundesliga 2026/27 match between VfB Stuttgart and Borussia Mönchengladbach at MHPArena on October 23, 2026 in Stuttgart, Germany. (Photo by Christian Kaspar-Bartke/Getty Images) Yes, but only at the right price and for a specific job. Leeds don’t need a replacement for Calvert-Lewin, whose box movement and aerial threat drive Farke’s crossing game through Jayden Bogle and James Justin. They need a second striker who finishes chances. Calvert-Lewin wasted several against Spurs, and Demirović’s expected goals suggest he reaches good positions and takes them. His defensive numbers suggest he would press from the front without breaking the 3-5-2’s shape. The risk is the delivery. A forward who loses three aerial duels in four makes a poor target for wing-back crosses, so Farke would need him running beyond Calvert-Lewin rather than competing with him. FotMob values him at €17m (about £15m), and the summer’s £26m now looks excessive for a 28-year-old. Krösche’s knowledge of him gives Milan an advantage, so Leeds can’t assume his eagerness to leave guarantees a move to Elland Road. If Stuttgart hold out, Leeds should spend on a different attacker. At around £15m he fixes a finishing problem; at £26m he becomes a risk.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team.
